issues.body: commit_plan independently commits selected.per_pattern and envelope.participating_sources, but never verifies that the envelope participation set equals the distinct sources assigned by the selection. A caller can remove a selected source from the envelope (or add an unrelated one) and still obtain Ok(PlanCommitment) containing contradictory selection and participation components. This undermines the advertised fail-closed construction and is especially material because the envelope is the declared leakage/accounting artifact.
issues.fix_hint: Derive the distinct selected source-id set from the committed patterns and require exact equality with the canonicalized envelope.participating_sources, returning DescriptorMismatch at PlanBinding on either omission or addition. Add real-pipeline mutation tests for both a dropped and an extra participant.
issues.title: Participation set is not cross-checked against selected source assignments

issues.body: commit_operators checks the disclose/hide flag and hidden operator class, but it canonicalizes declared.disclosed_operands without requiring that the list be empty when declared.disclosed is false. It therefore constructs a CommittedOperator with disclosed=false and non-empty disclosed_operands, despite the public field contract saying hidden operators have an empty list and the module claiming routing/envelope disagreement is refused. This creates a non-canonical contradictory representation and can invalidate the leakage statement that operands are disclosed only for Disclosed routes.
issues.fix_hint: Reject any hidden operator whose envelope has non-empty disclosed_operands with DescriptorMismatch at PlanBinding. Add a test that mutates a real assembled envelope by adding an operand to a hidden operator and asserts commit_plan fails.
issues.title: Hidden operators can carry disclosed operands

verdict.summary: The documentation is appropriately cautious about the audit-gated soundness boundary, and the tests exercise real Phase-2/3/4 construction. However, commit_plan does not fully validate that its three input artifacts describe one consistent plan. It accepts a participation set that disagrees with the selected per-pattern sources, and accepts disclosed operands on a hidden operator. Both cases contradict the stated fail-closed canonicalisation contract and can encode an internally inconsistent plan rather than rejecting it.
